headline: France's press suffocated Norwegian hopes from kickoff
story: France seized control in Boston with alarming speed. Two goals before the 21st minute—the 7th and 20th—established complete dominance. Aasgaard's immediate response at the 21st briefly suggested a contest, but France's superior press intensity and possession left Norway perpetually chasing. A third at the 32nd minute extinguished hope; a fourth in added time merely made the margin reflect the reality. France's ball recovery speed (12.7 seconds versus Norway's 17.9) meant they never lost the ebb and flow.

Norway out-created France on the xG ledger—1.45 to 1.05—yet paid for profligacy and poor execution under France's relentless press. Dembélé's transcendent 9.9 rating and Mbappé's 8.7 converted scarcity into dominance; Aasgaard (7.5) and Schjelderup (7.3) found few openings. Critically, Norway's 50th-minute 0.79-xG chance was saved—had that dropped, momentum could have shifted. Instead, Norway's forced turnovers (38) versus France's 43, combined with 17.9-second ball recovery against France's 12.7, meant relentless suffocation.
